title: Time Column Adder
description: Add and take away lengths of time in columns of hours, minutes and seconds, carry and borrow sixty and never ten, and line up seconds with their hundredths.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Add lengths of time in columns and carry at sixty, take one length from another and borrow at sixty, and line up seconds with their hundredths, so that any two lengths of time can be added, taken away, compared or shared.
writeup.look: A frame of hours, minutes and seconds columns with lengths of time stacked in it, carry and borrow tiles that are dragged across, and on the last phase seconds with two places for hundredths.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Time Column Adder' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of columns worked. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The frame of three columns, hours, minutes and seconds, stands at x 90, y 240, each column 200 wide and 340 tall, headed by its unit name in ink, with the column of the smaller unit at the right. The lengths of time the question gives are stacked in it in deep blue, labelled Given, one under another, and the right-hand column is lit amber until it is worked. The Regroup button stands at x 780, y 240 and the Break button under it at x 780, y 330. When a column reaches sixty, Regroup wraps the sixty into one of the next unit, 60 min into 1 h and 60 s into 1 min, as a violet tile, labelled Carry, and the child drags it into the next column to the left along y 215. Break turns 1 h into 60 min, or 1 min into 60 s, as a violet tile, labelled Regroup, and the part taken away is crossed out as it goes. On the fourth phase the seconds column grows a point and two places for hundredths, a thin ink rule locks the points of the two times in one line, and a grey zero, labelled Place holder, holds any empty place. Every answer is green, labelled Answer, with its units, along y 640. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a point key, a delete key, and keys for h, min and s. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the nine tools of this chapter share them. What the question gives, as a clock time, a length of time, a start date or a number of days, is deep blue, labelled Given or Start. What the working reaches, as an end time, a length of time, a converted time or a date, is green, labelled Answer, End or How long. The thin second hand and the seconds it counts are vermilion, labelled Second hand. One jump along a time line, and one regrouped unit carried or borrowed, are violet, labelled Jump, Carry or Regroup. On a day bar the half from noon until just before midnight is rose, labelled p.m., and the half from midnight until just before noon stays warm white inside its outline, labelled a.m. The hand, digit, column, jump or date being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open, labelled Place holder, and for nothing else. The hour hand and the minute hand, dials, tick marks, time lines, arrows, operation signs and step labels are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of the content colours, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The last working stays in the frame, with its carry or borrow tile where the child dropped it and the answer in green.

writeup.delight: On the second phase, as the minutes column fills to sixty, the sixty small cells fold into one violet tile that slides across into the hours column, and the minutes column starts again with what was left.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet worked. On the first phase the frame holds two lengths of time in hours and minutes, stacked in deep blue, with the minutes column lit amber. On the second the minutes of the two lengths add to more than sixty and the Regroup button waits beside the frame. On the third a length of time and a smaller one to take away are stacked with fewer minutes on top than below, and the Break button waits. On the fourth two race times in minutes and seconds with hundredths stand side by side, points not yet locked. One thing moves, once: the minutes column, the Break button or the seconds column gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any lengths of time stacked in the frame and added or taken away, with any two times set side by side. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on adding, carrying an hour, borrowing an hour and seconds with hundredths.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, no colour means good or bad. The miss empties the answer slot at once (every digit, every box, a picked choice), so it is empty through the traceback; the pad re-opens empty after it. CLUE FIRST (educator, 2026-11-18): the first and the second wrong answer show only a clue (the item's own miss line, then the phase's first ladder rung) with the pad open and empty again and nothing changed on the board; only from the THIRD wrong answer does the traceback run, showing the right answer and its steps. ORDER (educator, 2026-11-19): in a question with a carry or a borrow the child types the first column's total (the minutes, or the seconds) in its box and presses Enter; only then does the board play the regroup (the total struck, what stays written, a 1 tile) and the carry to the next column (or the break and the move for a take-away); then the child types the next column; what is already right stays in its box after a wrong column. Nothing (tile, chip, borrow) is drawn before the act that makes it, and the traceback replays the same order one act at a time.
tracebacks: Phase 1: each column is lit amber in turn from the right and its total is written in green under it, ending on the whole answer with its units

Phase 2: one step at a time, from the right: the column is added and its total written; then the regroup (the total struck, what stays written, a 1 tile); then the tile is carried to the next column; then that column is added with the carry, ending on the whole answer

Phase 3: one step at a time: the hour is broken (its top struck and the new top written), then the 60 minutes are moved to the minutes, then the minutes are taken away, then the hours, ending on the whole answer
Phase 4: the two points are locked in a line, each column is lit amber in turn from the right and the answer is written in green with its point in line; a shared time is dealt lane by lane

voice.opening: Columns of hours, minutes and seconds, ready to be added.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play: work any sum column by column, then tap New sum.
voice.onMiss: a question with a carry or a borrow is answered one column at a time from the right (the column's total first, Enter, then the regroup and the carry or the break and the move play on the board, then the next column); a wrong column is a wrong try: its own clue on the first wrong answer (add this column / take away in this column), a stronger clue on the second, the phase's second ladder rung together with the traceback (the right answer and its steps, in the same order) from the third; shown UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: You added and took away lengths of time and carried at sixty.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
